text:
The late vegetative stages (roughly V11 to V16) are a period of very rapid stem elongation and increasing height, along with high demand for nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K) as the plant builds the biomass it will need to fill a large ear. Internally, the tassel and ear are developing during this window: by about V12 the potential number of kernel rows on the ear is being set, and by around V16 (near tasseling) the potential ear length (kernels per row) is being determined.

Because these yield components are being fixed during this window, this stage is very sensitive to moisture, nutrient, or other stress -- stress here can permanently reduce the ear's potential size (row number or length) in a way that cannot be recovered later in the season, even if conditions improve afterward. This makes the late vegetative stage one of the most important windows for ensuring good fertility and water supply.
